1908 - President was Teddy Roosevelt. Potential successor is Taft. Roosevelt decides not to run for third term, endorses Taft, then ran against him 4 years later, but lost to Wilson. So no campaigning because Teddy thought he could do better.

1920 - President was Woodrow Wilson. Potential successor is Cox. Wilson calls Cox's campaign a joke and wants to run for a third term. Thus no campaigning there. Cox loses, Wilson dies.

1928 - President is Calvin Coolidge (After Harding dies in office). Potential successor is Hoover. Coolidge endorses Hoover, but lacks the energy to campaign after being heavily affected by the death of his father and son.

1932 - Hoover loses second term election to FDR.

1945 - FDR dies, Truman sworn in. (so no campaigning yet). During Truman's next two elections, not sure why Hoover didn't campaign for him (maybe age? maybe they didn't need him?)

1952 - Eisenhower wins.

1960 - President is Eisenhower. Potential successor is Nixon. "Give me a week" to think of a Nixon idea. Eisenhower pretty much said his VP, Nixon, never had a good idea. Not a very warm relationship, so no campaigning there

1963 - Kennedy is shot, LBJ sworn in.

1968 - President is Lydon B Johnson. Potential successor is Humphrey. Humphrey breaks with LBJ: "Not only did Johnson not campaign with Humphrey; he made things more difficult for him". Vietnam was a hell of a thing

1976 - President is Ford. Ford loses to Carter; Ford had assumed office after Nixon resigned following Watergate: Carter didn't have a democrat president to stump for him because LBJ was dead, and I don't think the Ford camp wanted Nixon at all.

1988 - President is Reagan. Potential successor is Bush. Reagan endorses Bush, rhymes with "rush": At 72 and with his alzheimers setting in, the Bush campaign didn't want him actively stumping

2000 - President is Clinton. Potential successor is Gore. Gore distances from Clinton: Gore didn't like Clinton and his improprieties, probably didn't want an impeached president stumping for him.

2008 - President is George W. Bush. Potential successor is John McCain. McCain didn't want him to be part of the campaign due to all the bad publicity around the wars and economy.

So it seems that, in most cases, the sitting president wasn't really impressed with their success or, if they were, they couldn't get out and stump for them. So it may be unprecedented, but not because it's ethically wrong or illegal, just because there haven't been the right circumstances in recent history. We could go back and research earlier than the 1900s but I don't think it's worth the time. What will be interesting is to see if maybe the Clintons and Obamas have worked out a deal for Hillary to be Pres, then endorse/stump for Michelle or something like that.
